background.task:
I tested the **browser4-media** plugin end-to-end on three w3schools pages plus an HLS control page, using only `./b4w.ps1` commands.

**Setup note (the dominant obstacle):** the media plugin was **not installed** in the running backend — `plugin list` showed 4 plugins (captcha, images, markdown, swarm) and `GET /mcp/tools` listed 304 tools with zero `media_*` entries. I installed the locally-built JAR (`browser4-plugins/browser4-media/target/browser4-media-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar`), ran `./b4w.ps1 stop`, and the next command auto-started the backend with the plugin loaded (7 tools: `media_detect_videos`, `media_download`, `media_get_info`, `media_process`, `media_extract_audio`, `media_trim`, `media_compress`). The JAR is newer than all plugin sources, so the checked-out code was tested. Both `tool call media_detect_videos` and the dotted `tool call media.detectVideos` work, as does the documented `plugin-media detectVideos` / `plugin media` form.

**Step 2 — `html5_video.asp`:** `media.detectVideos` returned **4 unique sources**:

| # | tag | source | MIME | dims | controls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `video` | `https://www.w3schools.com/html/mov_bbb.mp4` | *(absent)* | 320×176 | true |
| 1 | `source` | `mov_bbb.ogg` → resolved `…/mov_bbb.ogg` | video/ogg | 320×176 | true |
| 2 | `video` | `data:video/mp4;base64,…` (1142 chars) | *(absent)* | null | false |
| 3 | `source` | `data:video/webm;base64,…` (271 chars) | video/webm | null | false |

Breakdown: `<video>` tags = 2 reported (3 exist in the DOM), `<source>` children = 2 reported (6 exist), **iframe embeds = 0** (none of the page's 19 iframes is a player embed). **No HLS or DASH streams** were detected (none are present). Ground truth via `eval`: the main document has 2 `<video>` elements each with 2 `<source>` children (`mov_bbb.mp4`, `mov_bbb.ogg`), and a same-origin `about:blank` video-ad iframe (Viously) contributes the two `data:` URIs. The tool reports **unique URLs, not elements** — URL dedup collapses the duplicates and, because the `<video>` is emitted before its children, the `<source type="video/mp4">` entry is dropped, so **no entry carries the MP4's MIME type**, and the ad unit's videos appear indistinguishable from page videos.

**Step 3 — download:** `media_download` on the detected MP4 returned `success=true, bytesDownloaded=788493, contentType=video/mp4, durationMs=4812`. The file exists on disk (788,493 bytes, `file` → "ISO Media, MP4 v2"). By default it landed in `<runtime-bundle>/downloads/media/mov_bbb.mp4` — i.e. inside `browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/target/runtime-bundle/_work/…`, deep in the build output tree. Passing `outputPath`/`filename` works (absolute paths anywhere, missing dirs created), which is the workaround for a sane location; `config` exposes no `media.*` key.

**Step 4 — `html_youtube.asp`:** detection returned only the ad-iframe `data:` URIs — **no YouTube embed**. This is correct behaviour: the page's `youtube.com/embed` URLs exist only as escaped code samples (`<iframe …>`); the rendered DOM has 8 iframes, none from YouTube. Control test on `tryit.asp?filename=tryhtml_youtubeiframe` (a live embed) detected the iframe correctly (`isIframe=true`, `420×345`, `https://www.youtube.com/embed/tgbNymZ7vqY`), so the iframe path works.

**Step 5 — `tryit.asp?filename=tryhtml5_video`:** `eval` showed the main document has 0 `<video>` elements while the same-origin `#iframeResult` frame contains 1 `<video width=400 controls>` with two `<source>` children. `media.detectVideos` (backend view) found that iframe's video (`mov_bbb.mp4` + `mov_bbb.ogg`) plus the ad-frame `data:` URIs — same-origin iframe scanning works, but results carry no indication of which frame they came from.

**Step 6 — `media.getInfo`** on the downloaded file: `format=mov,mp4,m4a,3gp,3g2,mj2`, `duration=10.026667 s`, `320×176`, `codec=h264`, `bitrate=629116`, `streams=4` (0: video h264 320×176, 1: audio aac, 2: audio aac, 3: data bin_data). Local `ffprobe` returns byte-identical values.

**Extra probe:** on the hls.js demo (a page actively playing an HLS stream), detection reported a single `blob:https://…` video with `isHls=false` — the m3u8 URL was never surfaced, so HLS detection does not work for the standard hls.js/MSE case.
background.executionContext:
**Preparation:** `pwd` (repo root) → `./b4w.ps1 help` → read `skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md` in full → `--help plugins|plugin|plugin install|plugin list|plugin info|tool call` → `plugin list` → `./b4w.ps1 status`.

**Environment discovery:** `curl http://localhost:8282/mcp/tools` (304 tools, no media), `find` for the plugin module, read `browser4-plugins/browser4-media/README.md` + manifest, inspected the runtime bundle's `plugins/` dir, checked jar-vs-source timestamps, `which ffmpeg ffprobe`.

**Key commands:** `plugin install browser4-plugins/browser4-media/target/browser4-media-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar` → `stop` → `plugin list` (media loaded) → `-s media-eval goto <url>` ×4 → `tool call media_detect_videos` ×5 → `tool call media.detectVideos` (dotted alias test) → `tool call media_download` ×4 (default dir; explicit `outputPath`; outside-repo path; 404 URL) → `tool call media_get_info` ×2 (real file; missing file) → `eval --json` with inline and `--file` JS probes (main-doc/iframe DOM audit, HLS state) → `plugin` (bare) → `plugin media`, `plugin media_detect`, `plugin-media detectVideos`, `plugin-media download --url … --outputPath …`, `plugin-media --help`, `plugin-media detectVideos --help` → `config list` → `plugin info browser4-media` → `curl /mcp/tools/<name>`, `POST /mcp`, `/mcp/tool/…` (all 404) → local `ffprobe -show_format -show_streams` cross-check → `curl` of the raw w3schools HTML to explain the missing YouTube embed.

**Decisions/workarounds:** (1) installed the plugin from the repo build output and restarted via `stop` + auto-start because the tools were entirely absent; (2) used a named session `-s media-eval`; (3) used `eval --file` to dodge nested-quote issues in JS probes; (4) added a live-YouTube control page because the assigned page has no live embed, so "not detected" alone would have been ambiguous; (5) used explicit `outputPath` to keep downloaded artifacts in the run scratch dir; (6) deleted the one file I had written to `%TEMP%` while probing whether out-of-repo paths are accepted.

**Evidence:** all raw outputs are under `.test-sessions/20261015T0901431699046Z/` (`help-full.txt`, `plugin-list*.txt`, `step2-*` … `step7-*`, `plugin-domains.txt`, and the consolidated `FINDINGS-SUMMARY.md`).



**Note on state changed during this run:** I installed `browser4-media-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar` into the workspace's runtime bundle (`plugins/`), which persists after this session. To revert: `./b4w.ps1 plugin remove browser4-media` followed by `./b4w.ps1 stop`. All scratch artifacts (evidence files, JS probes, downloaded media) are under `.test-sessions/20261015T0901431699046Z/`; the one file written to `%TEMP%` while testing out-of-repo download paths was removed.

assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all six task steps were carried out and every requested datum was produced (detection inventory, MP4 download verified on disk, YouTube-page behaviour, iframe evaluation, ffprobe metadata), but only after a manual plugin install and backend restart that the task setup did not anticipate; two of the sub-questions (HLS/DASH detection, YouTube embed detection) required additional control pages to answer honestly.
assessment.successRate: 85% — the media workflow itself was reached on the first try once installed and every command returned useful data; markdown-quality answers for steps 4 and 6 were only possible after extra investigation because the page had no live embed and because HLS detection silently failed.
assessment.majorBlockers: The browser4-media plugin was not installed in the running backend: none of the seven media.* tools existed (304 MCP tools, zero media_*), and nothing in `plugin list`, `plugin info`, `tool call --help` or the SKILL.md said a media plugin existed or how to load it. The task only proceeded after `plugin install <repo jar>` + `stop` + auto-restart. Secondary blocker: the assigned YouTube page contains no live YouTube embed (only escaped code samples), so the 'is the embed detected' question could not be answered from that page alone.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: 1) The task's tool names (media.detectVideos) match neither the CLI's documented snake_case convention nor the `plugin-media` command form, and there is no command that lists a plugin's tools or their arguments — the only schema discovery is triggering an error. 2) `plugin-media --help` answers 'Unknown command' for a command that works. 3) Detection output silently merges same-origin iframes (including video-ad creatives) with no frame attribution, and dedupes by URL so element counts and the MP4's MIME type vanish. 4) The default download lands deep inside the build-output tree with no config key to change it. 5) The bare `plugin` listing is a 115-entry mix of core tools and mangled names (base_u_r, nano_d_o_m).
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make the media plugin reachable out of the box — bundle it, or have startup/status report 'built but not installed' plugins with the exact install command. 2) Add real tool discovery: `tool list`/`tool describe`, plugin tool names in `plugin list`, and working `--help` for dynamic plugin commands. 3) Give detection results frame attribution (frameUrl/depth) and fix the dedup so MIME/counts survive. 4) Make the download directory configurable and clearly reported (absolute path, stable location). 5) Fix HLS detection for MSE-based players (or mark blob/MSE sources as opaque) and truncate data: URIs in output.

issues.title: browser4-media is not installed (or bundled); every media.* tool is missing out of the box

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 plugin list
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8282/mcp/tools | grep -o -i '"media[a-z0-9_\.]*"'   # no output
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_detect_videos
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The media tools are available after setup, or the CLI says which plugin provides them and how to install it (the main help does describe the generic install recipe).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: plugin list shows only captcha/images/markdown/swarm; GET /mcp/tools lists 304 tools with zero media_* names; calling media.detectVideos fails with no hint that a plugin supplies it. Workaround that succeeded: ./b4w.ps1 plugin install browser4-plugins/browser4-media/target/browser4-media-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar, then ./b4w.ps1 stop (next command auto-started the backend and loaded the plugin; 7 media tools appeared).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The runtime bundle only ever receives browser4-swarm: build-runtime-bundle.ps1 copies the swarm JAR explicitly into <bundle>/plugins and leaves every other first-party plugin to a manual install. browser4-media compiles to browser4-plugins/browser4-media/target/browser4-media-4.14.1-SNAPSHOT.jar but nothing in the dev-mode startup path scans that directory or warns that a repo plugin is present-but-not-installed, so the checked-out media code is unreachable until a human reads plugin install --help or the main help's 'Server plugins' section.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/build-runtime-bundle.ps1 (swarm-only bundling, ~lines 985-1167); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (handle_plugin_list, ~line 21704)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Make dev-mode startup (or `status`/`doctor`) compare browser4-plugins/*/target/*.jar against the bundle's plugins/ dir and print an actionable 'built but not installed' warning with the exact install command.
- Consider bundling browser4-media with the dev-mode bundle the way swarm is bundled, since it has no external service dependency (unlike captcha).
- If neither is desirable, name the first-party plugins and their tool domains in the main help so a user learns media.* exists at all.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: `plugin-<domain> <method> --help` reports the command as unknown, so plugin tools have no help

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval plugin-media detectVideos --help
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval plugin-media --help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The media domain's method list and arguments, matching `browser4-cli --help <command>` for static commands.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Prints "Plugin tool domain 'media' is not a static CLI command. ... Unknown command: plugin-media" followed by the full 350-line generic help — while the identical command without --help runs successfully. There is no way to enumerate a plugin domain's methods or arguments from the CLI.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Dynamic plugin commands are resolved at dispatch time from the plugin registry, but the --help path only consults the static command table/help.rs generators, so a dynamic name falls through to unknown-command handling and the generic banner. The method list itself is only ever exposed by the bare `plugin` command, which is not what a user types next to the command they are curious about.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (command dispatch/help handling for plugin-* names); cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs:generate_help()
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Resolve `plugin-<domain>` (and `plugin <domain>`) in the help path before the static lookup fails, and print the domain's methods with their signatures from the ToolSpec registry.
- Support `plugin-<domain> <method> --help` to render the individual ToolSpec (arguments, defaults, description).
- Route the unknown-command path away from dumping the whole help when the name matches an installed plugin domain.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: detectVideos mixes same-origin iframe and ad-unit videos into one flat list with no frame attribution

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval goto "https://www.w3schools.com/html/html5_video.asp"
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_detect_videos
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Results attributable to the frame they came from, or ad/third-party iframes excluded — a user scanning 'the page' should not receive video-ad creatives as page videos.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: 4 entries; entries 2-3 are data:video/mp4;base64,… and data:video/webm;base64,… belonging to a Viously video-ad unit inside a same-origin about:blank iframe. They carry tagName 'video'/'source', isIframe:false, and there is no frameUrl/depth field, so they are indistinguishable from page content. The DOM audit shows 3 video elements across 2 documents versus 4 reported entries.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: DETECTION_SCRIPT runs __b4_scan_videos(document) and then loops over every iframe whose contentDocument is readable (about:blank iframes inherit the parent origin, so ad units qualify) into the same accumulator; the VideoSource data class has no field recording which document/frame an entry came from, and no ad/third-party filter is applied.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/service/VideoDetector.kt (VideoSource data class; same-origin iframe loop at the end of DETECTION_SCRIPT)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add `frameUrl`, `frameDepth` (and optionally `isCrossOrigin`) to VideoSource and populate them per document during the scan.
- Add an option (e.g. `includeIframes=false`) or at least flag entries that came from a nested document so agents can filter them.
- Consider skipping iframes whose URL is about:blank or matches known ad domains by default.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: URL dedup collapses per-element results and silently drops the primary video's MIME type

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval goto "https://www.w3schools.com/html/html5_video.asp"
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_detect_videos
eval "document.querySelectorAll('video').length + ' videos / ' + document.querySelectorAll('video source').length + ' sources'"  # 2 videos / 4 sources
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Either one entry per DOM element, or a deduplicated view that preserves the fields (notably the MIME `type`) and the element count.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The main document's 2 <video> + 4 <source> collapse into 2 entries; the MP4 entry has no `type` at all even though the markup declares <source src="mov_bbb.mp4" type="video/mp4">. The type-carrying <source> was discarded because its resolvedUrl equals the <video>'s currentSrc and the <video> (type null) was emitted first. Reported 'total sources' (4) therefore matches neither element count (6) nor URL count in the DOM.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: parseResult() calls distinctBy { it.resolvedUrl ?: it.srcUrl } after the JS has already suppressed duplicates first-seen-wins, and __b4_scan_videos emits the <video> before iterating its <source> children, so the richer entry never survives. isHls/isDash are likewise computed per element from src only.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/service/VideoDetector.kt:parseResult() and DETECTION_SCRIPT (video/source iteration order)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Prefer the entry with more information when deduplicating (keep the first non-null `type`, posterUrl, dimensions) instead of first-seen-wins.
- Add a `duplicateCount`/`elementCount` field, or a `distinct=false` mode returning every element.
- Emit <source> children before the parent <video>, or merge source metadata into the parent entry.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: HLS streams played through hls.js/MSE are reported as blob: sources with isHls=false

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval goto "https://hlsjs.video-dev.org/demo/"
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_detect_videos
# page state: typeof Hls === 'function', Hls.instances === undefined, video.src === blob:https://hlsjs.video-dev.org/…
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The HLS manifest URL is surfaced (or at least isHls=true), since the page is actively playing https://test-streams.mux.dev/x36xhzz/x36xhzz.m3u8.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Single entry: srcUrl/resolvedUrl = blob:https://hlsjs.video-dev.org/8e7f22de-…, isHls=false, isDash=false. The blob: URL is unusable for media.download, so the detection is a dead end for the most common HLS deployment.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The HLS branch only reads the static `Hls.instances` array (undefined on this page) and never inspects the manifest URL — yet the m3u8 is discoverable in the page (URL query string / input value). MSE-loaded media always exposes only blob: URLs to the DOM, so an element-based probe cannot see the stream URL without the player's own state.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/service/VideoDetector.kt (final section of DETECTION_SCRIPT: Hls.instances / dashjs.getMediaPlayers branch)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Track Hls/dashjs instances more robustly (hook the constructor or read Hls.DefaultConfig/MediaSource, or scan for .m3u8/.mpd URLs in page text, script contents and the page URL query) instead of relying on Hls.instances.
- Mark blob:/mediasource: sources as 'opaque (MSE)' so callers know the URL cannot be downloaded.
- Add a test that loads a page with a data-driven HLS player and asserts isHls=true.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Default download destination is inside the runtime-bundle build tree and cannot be configured from the CLI

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_download --json '{"url":"https://www.w3schools.com/html/mov_bbb.mp4"}'
# filePath = .../browser4-apps/browser4-bundle/target/runtime-bundle/_work/browser4-bundle-runtime-windows-x64/browser4-bundle-runtime-windows-x64/downloads/media/mov_bbb.mp4
./b4w.ps1 config list
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Downloads land somewhere the user can find (a documented, stable directory) and the location can be set through the CLI's config surface.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Files are written relative to the backend process's working directory — the runtime bundle tree under target/runtime-bundle/_work/…, which is regenerated by bundles builds. config list exposes only server/timeout/proxy/session/extension_id, and server-side keys are limited to agent.llm.maxRequestTokens and agent.token.budget.total, so media.download.dir cannot be changed without editing backend config files. The README's 'downloads/media' implies the caller's working directory.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: MediaConfig's media.download.dir defaults to the relative path 'downloads/media', resolved against the JVM's CWD (the bundle root in dev mode). The CLI bundles only the five CLI defaults plus two agent keys, so no supported path reaches plugin properties.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/config/MediaConfig.kt (media.download.dir) and service/MediaDownloader.kt; cli/browser4-cli src (config key allow-list)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Default to a stable user-visible directory (e.g. <workspace app-data>/downloads/media) and print the absolute path prominently in the result (the value is currently only visible inside the embedded DownloadResult string).
- Allow arbitrary server-side keys such as media.download.dir through `config set`, or document the config file/property to edit.
- Consider a `tool call ... --out <dir>`-style CLI-level output redirection so callers control where files land on their own machine.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Full base64 data: URIs are echoed verbatim in detection output

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_detect_videos   # on w3schools pages whose ad iframe uses data: URIs
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Opaque inline payloads summarised (e.g. 'data:video/mp4;base64,<2900 B>') so the payload stays readable and cheap for an LLM context.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The 1142-char and 271-char base64 strings are printed twice each (srcUrl and resolvedUrl); a 4-source page produces 3.4 KB of output dominated by base64 that cannot be used for a download anyway.

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/service/VideoDetector.kt (DETECTION_SCRIPT result assembly) / MediaToolExecutor result serialization

issues.title: Tool-call error help prints the tool signature twice

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s media-eval tool call media_get_info --json '{"filePath":"D:/tmp/missing.mp4"}'
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The signature appears once, followed by the description.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body:
"[INVALID_ARGUMENT] media_get_info failed: File not found: … help: Get media file metadata (…) using ffprobe.
media.getInfo(filePath: String)

media.getInfo(filePath: String)

Returns detailed information…" — the signature line is repeated.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The framework already prepends the tool signature when composing a usage-error help block, while the plugin's ToolSpec.help string begins with the same signature line; the same pattern exists in the captcha/images/markdown plugins, so every plugin tool error is affected.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-plugins/browser4-media/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/media/tools/MediaToolExecutor.kt (help strings, e.g. the getInfo spec at ~line 166); browser4-rest MCPToolController.buildErrorMessage (~line 2040)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:

issues.title: `plugin` domain listing mixes in core tools and mangles camelCase names

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 plugin
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The installed plugins' tool domains and methods (e.g. media -> detectVideos, download, getInfo…), as the heading 'Available plugin commands' and the help text promise.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: 115 entries that include core built-in tools (click, fill, hover, eval, navigate, screenshot, scroll, select, type, upload…) plus garbled conversions of camelCase API names: base_u_r (baseURL), document_u_r (documentURI), nano_d_o_m, outer_h_t_m. media_download is absent from the list although `plugin media_download` / `plugin-media download` work.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The listing is generated by snake_casing every registered MCP tool name and truncating to two underscore-separated tokens; the transformation is lossy for names containing acronyms (baseURL -> base_u_r) and blind to whether the tool comes from a plugin or the core driver, and the source list does not cover every method (media.download).

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (bare `plugin` listing handler)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Derive the list from the plugin registry's ToolSpec domains (plugin-provided only, or a clearly separated second section for core tools) instead of snake_casing raw tool names.
